quests.activeVoice: Please keep this door closed at all times.
quests.passiveVoice: This door is to be kept closed at all times.
quests.targetSentence: Please keep this door closed at all times.
quests.ruleExplanation: This is an imperative with an understood subject, you: (you) keep this door closed. Since a command directs someone to act, it counts as active voice even without a stated subject. The idea can be rephrased as an instruction in passive style: This door is to be kept closed at all times.
quests.nativeTip: Commands like this have an understood you as the doer. Ask who is being told to keep the door closed.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Please keep this door closed at all times. ⇄ Passive: This door is to be kept closed at all times.

quests.targetSentence: Passengers are requested to fasten their seatbelts before takeoff.
quests.ruleExplanation: Passengers (receiver) are requested - a polite passive alternative to a direct command, with the airline as the implied but unnamed requester. Active form, as a direct instruction: Please fasten your seatbelt before takeoff.
quests.nativeTip: Passengers aren't requesting anything here - something is being asked of them. Look for are requested plus a passive infinitive.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Please fasten your seatbelt before takeoff. ⇄ Passive: Passengers are requested to fasten their seatbelts before takeoff.

quests.targetSentence: This medication must be taken with food, not on an empty stomach.
quests.ruleExplanation: This medication (receiver) must be taken - modal passive is often preferred for instructions and warnings, since the rule matters more than who follows it. Active form: You must take this medication with food, not on an empty stomach.
quests.nativeTip: Medication doesn't take itself. Look for must be plus a past participle, a common pattern for instructions.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: You must take this medication with food, not on an empty stomach. ⇄ Passive: This medication must be taken with food, not on an empty stomach.

quests.nativeTip: Visitors don't advise themselves. Look for are advised plus a passive infinitive.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Management advises visitors to wear closed-toe shoes on the factory floor. ⇄ Passive: Visitors are advised to wear closed-toe shoes on the factory floor.

quests.conceptTitle: Perspective Rotator: Modal Verbs Active (No Passive Possible)
quests.activeVoice: Staff must clock in before starting any shift.
quests.passiveVoice: No passive form exists - clock in has no object here, so there is no receiver to become the subject.
quests.targetSentence: Staff must clock in before starting any shift.
quests.ruleExplanation: Staff is the doer of must clock in, modal active - clock in has no separate object here, so this stays active in either direction, since there's nothing to receive the action and become a passive subject.
quests.nativeTip: Find the doer right before must clock in.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Staff must clock in before starting any shift. ⇄ Passive: No passive form exists - clock in has no object here, so there is no receiver to become the subject.

quests.targetSentence: This equipment should be switched off after each use.

quests.nativeTip: Equipment doesn't switch itself off. Look for should be plus a past participle.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: You should switch this equipment off after each use. ⇄ Passive: This equipment should be switched off after each use.

quests.activeVoice: The librarian gave me a temporary card for the summer program.
quests.passiveVoice: I was given a temporary card for the summer program by the librarian.
quests.targetSentence: The librarian gave me a temporary card for the summer program.
quests.ruleExplanation: The librarian is the doer of gave, which takes two objects here: me (indirect) and a temporary card (direct). Active voice keeps both after the verb. Passive voice usually promotes the indirect object instead: I was given a temporary card for the summer program.
quests.nativeTip: This verb has two objects: me and a temporary card. Find the doer, right before gave.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: The librarian gave me a temporary card for the summer program. ⇄ Passive: I was given a temporary card for the summer program by the librarian.

quests.activeVoice: The librarian gave me a temporary card for the summer program.
quests.passiveVoice: I was given a temporary card for the summer program by the librarian.
quests.targetSentence: I was given a temporary card for the summer program by the librarian.
quests.ruleExplanation: I (receiver of the giving) am the subject even though a temporary card is what was actually handed over - with two-object verbs like give, English usually makes the person, not the item, the passive subject. Active form: The librarian gave me a temporary card for the summer program.
quests.nativeTip: Notice the subject I isn't performing was given - it's receiving something. Look for was given plus the remaining object, a temporary card.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: The librarian gave me a temporary card for the summer program. ⇄ Passive: I was given a temporary card for the summer program by the librarian.

quests.activeVoice: The librarian gave a temporary card to me for the summer program.
quests.passiveVoice: A temporary card was given to me for the summer program.
quests.targetSentence: A temporary card was given to me for the summer program.
quests.ruleExplanation: A temporary card (receiver) is the subject this time, with to me showing who benefited - this is the less common but still correct passive option for two-object verbs, using to before the person. Active form: The librarian gave a temporary card to me for the summer program.
quests.nativeTip: Compare this with the previous sentence - here the item, not the person, is the subject. Look for was given, followed by to me.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: The librarian gave a temporary card to me for the summer program. ⇄ Passive: A temporary card was given to me for the summer program.

quests.targetSentence: The bank sent him a new debit card after the old one expired.

quests.nativeTip: Find the doer right before sent, and notice the two objects: him and a new debit card.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: The bank sent him a new debit card after the old one expired. ⇄ Passive: He was sent a new debit card after the old one expired by the bank.

quests.conceptTitle: Perspective Rotator: Two-Object Verb Active (Negative Subject)
quests.activeVoice: Nobody told the new hires about the fire drill schedule.
quests.passiveVoice: The new hires weren't told about the fire drill schedule.
quests.targetSentence: Nobody told the new hires about the fire drill schedule.
quests.ruleExplanation: Nobody is actually the doer here, and told takes two objects: the new hires and about the fire drill schedule - so despite the negative-sounding subject, this sentence is grammatically active. The new hires can become the passive subject instead: The new hires weren't told about the fire drill schedule.
quests.nativeTip: Wait - check carefully. Does nobody perform an action, or does someone receive one? Look at who ends up without information.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Nobody told the new hires about the fire drill schedule. ⇄ Passive: The new hires weren't told about the fire drill schedule.

quests.activeVoice: Nobody told the new hires about the fire drill schedule.
quests.passiveVoice: The new hires weren't told about the fire drill schedule.
quests.targetSentence: The new hires weren't told about the fire drill schedule.
quests.ruleExplanation: The new hires (receiver) weren't told - negative passive with a two-object verb, promoting the people rather than the information. No specific person is blamed. Active form: Nobody told the new hires about the fire drill schedule.
quests.nativeTip: The new hires didn't tell anyone anything - something was withheld from them. Look for weren't told.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Nobody told the new hires about the fire drill schedule. ⇄ Passive: The new hires weren't told about the fire drill schedule.

quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: The city awarded the contractor a substantial bonus for finishing early. ⇄ Passive: The contractor was awarded a substantial bonus for finishing early by the city.

quests.conceptTitle: Perspective Rotator: Active with Embedded Passive Clause
quests.activeVoice: Once the alarm is reset, staff can resume normal operations.
quests.passiveVoice: Normal operations can be resumed by staff once the alarm is reset.
quests.targetSentence: Once the alarm is reset, staff can resume normal operations.
quests.ruleExplanation: The main clause here is active: staff is the doer of can resume, even though the earlier clause, the alarm is reset, is passive. Judge each clause separately rather than the whole sentence at once. Passive version of the main clause: Normal operations can be resumed by staff once the alarm is reset.
quests.nativeTip: Find the doer right before can resume, ignoring the earlier passive clause is reset.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Once the alarm is reset, staff can resume normal operations. ⇄ Passive: Normal operations can be resumed by staff once the alarm is reset.

quests.nativeTip: Reporters didn't tell anyone anything here. Look for were told, a two-object verb in passive form.
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Officials told the reporters very little about the ongoing investigation. ⇄ Passive: The reporters were told very little about the ongoing investigation.

quests.targetSentence: The employees received their paychecks a day early this month.

Passive version, if the giver is emphasized instead: Paychecks were issued to the employees a day early this month.
quests.nativeTip: Receive looks similar to a passive idea, but check: does received show something being done to the employees, or something they did themselves?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: The employees received their paychecks a day early this month. ⇄ Passive: Paychecks were issued to the employees a day early this month.

quests.visualAnchor: 🔄 Active: Staff handed guests a welcome package as soon as they checked in. ⇄ Passive: Guests were handed a welcome package as soon as they checked in.
